evals.prompt: Write an email to recruiter Dana Ruiz at Northbeam Staffing about her post on 40 open construction roles. (resume.md, voice/VOICE.md and voice/rules.json present; communications/LOG.md shows no prior contact.)
evals.expected_output: Reads the log (no prior contact), drafts a short email with a subject line from the resume facts only, runs scripts/check_voice.py with voice/rules.json on the email channel and revises until it passes, runs verify_no_fabrication against the resume, and saves the draft for the user to send. Does not ask for a 15-minute call (the user's rules ban it). Does not send anything.

evals.prompt: Draft a LinkedIn connection note to recruiter Sam Ortiz. (recruiters.json says linkedin_connected: true and an intro email was sent on 2026-10-15.)
evals.expected_output: Reads the records first, sees the user is already connected and already emailed Sam, and does not draft a connection request. Says so and offers a direct message that follows up on the email instead.

evals.prompt: Write a message to a recruiter at Globex about their estimator openings. (resume.md present; there is no voice/ folder.)
evals.expected_output: Notes there is no voice profile, drafts in plain professional prose from the resume, runs the anti-fabrication gate, and offers to build a voice profile (one question at a time, or starting from references/rules-starter.json). Does not invent a voice or claim the draft was voice-checked.

evals.prompt: Tell the Acme recruiter I have ten years of estimating experience. (resume.md shows about two years as an estimator.)
evals.expected_output: Refuses to state ten years: the resume supports about two. The gate flags the new number. Offers a truthful line built from the real estimating experience, and asks the user before adding any claim the resume does not support.

values: ten years of estimating experience at
